CHIEF COMPLAINT
Patient presents ready to quit smoking.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old patient with long-standing smoking history starting in high school with experimental use that progressed to daily smoking. Currently smoking 1.5 packs per day, with first cigarette within one hour of waking. Patient previously attempted to quit by going cold turkey and was successful for almost a year but relapsed due to work-related stress from layoffs and increased responsibilities. Patient is now motivated to quit due to impending fatherhood. Patient reports recently starting meditation and joining a gym as stress management strategies. Patient interested in nicotine patch as smoking cessation aid based on friends' recommendations. Quit date planned for next Monday, which is patient's birthday.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type two diabetes, history of gout, cardiac murmur (2/6 systolic murmur noted on prior exams, currently being monitored).

MEDICATIONS
Allopurinol for gout management.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is 44 years old, currently employed (retained job during recent workplace layoffs), about to become a father. Wife pregnant with a daughter. Patient recently joined gym and has started meditation practice.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure 128/88 mmHg, heart rate 68 bpm, respirations 16, oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Heart: Regular rate and rhythm with 2/6 systolic murmur appreciated, consistent with prior exams. Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally, no expiratory wheezes, no rales or rhonchi. Neck: No lymphadenopathy, no carotid bruits appreciated.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine dependence: Patient counseled on benefits of smoking cessation particularly given history of gout and type two diabetes. Starting 21 mg nicotine patch on Monday (quit date). Instructed to change patch location daily to avoid skin irritation. Plan to gradually decrease patch dosage over time. Patient advised to monitor stress levels related to work and upcoming birth. Encouraged to continue exercise routine and consider meditation and yoga for stress management. Follow-up appointment in two weeks to reassess and reevaluate dosage.
2. Type two diabetes: Continue management with diet and exercise. Hemoglobin A1c to be ordered for next blood draw, results to be reviewed at follow-up visit in two weeks.
3. Gout: Continue allopurinol. Patient counseled to continue monitoring foods that exacerbate uric acid levels.
